source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 1016 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Article heading
sections.text:
ARTICLE 1016.

PD 1016.

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1016.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 1016 was established by Ordinance No. 31226, passed by the Dallas City Council on May 22, 2019. (Ord. 31226)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1016.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 1016 is established on property located on the southwest corner of Samuell Boulevard and Hunnicut Road. The size of PD 1016 is approximately 26.034 acres. (Ord. 31226)

sections.title: Vision Statement
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1016.103. VISION STATEMENT.

This district is envisioned to be a vibrant single family development providing different types of units. The development is intended to provide for housing alternatives in the area and to become a cohesive neighborhood, featuring common open space, an amenity center, and a focus on being pedestrian oriented. (Ord. 31226)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1016.104. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In this article:

(1) MEWS COURTYARD means a public or private area primarily for pedestrians that provides access to buildings and connection throughout the district.

(2) OPEN SPACE means an area used for recreational and gathering purposes that is accessible to all occupants of the Property and contains only landscaping, hardscaping, pedestrian amenities, and structures with omitted walls. This may include mews courtyards and detention areas.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. 31226)

sections.title: Exhibits
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1016.105. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this article:

(1) Exhibit 1016A: conceptual plan.

(2) Exhibit 1016B: street section. (Ord. 31226)

sections.title: Conceptual Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1016.106. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit 1016A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the conceptual plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 31226)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1016.107. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

A development plan must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of any building permit to authorize work in this district. If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 31226)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1016.108. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in this section, the only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the R- 7.5(A) Single Family District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District is subject to DIR in this district; etc.

(b) The following additional main uses are permitted by right:

-- Private recreation center, club, or area. -- Private street or alley. (Ord. 31226)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1016.109. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217. (Ord. 31226)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1016.110. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) Front yard.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, minimum front yard is 10 feet.

(2) For single family structures on lots containing a minimum of 4,000 square feet, minimum front yard is 20 feet.

(3) For single family structures on lots containing a minimum of 1,500 square feet and a maximum of 3,999 square feet, minimum front yard is five feet.

(4) For corner lots with two street frontages of unequal distance, the shorter frontage is governed by this section, and the longer frontage is governed by the side yard regulations in Section 51P-1016.110(b).

(5) If a lot runs from a private street to a public street, and has double frontage, a minimum 20-foot setback must be provided from the lot line abutting the private street and a minimum 10-foot setback must be provided from the lot line abutting the public street.

(b) Side yard.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, minimum side yard is five feet.

(2) For single family structures on lots containing a minimum of 1,500 square feet and a maximum of 3,999 square feet, a minimum three-foot side yard is required on one side of the lot. No minimum side yard is required on the other side of the same lot.

(c) Rear yard.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, no minimum rear yard is required.

(2) For single family structures on lots containing a minimum of 4,000 square feet, minimum front yard is 10 feet.

(3) For single family structures on lots containing a minimum of 1,500 square feet and a maximum of 3,999 square feet, minimum front yard is five feet.

(d) Mews courtyard setback. A minimum five-foot setback must be provided measured from the Property line abutting the mews courtyard.

(e) Density. Maximum number of dwelling units is 240.

(f) Floor area ratio. No maximum floor area ratio.

(g) Height. Maximum structure height is 36 feet.

(h) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is:

(1) 53 percent for residential structures on lots containing a minimum of 4,000 square feet;

(2) 74 percent for residential structures on lots containing a minimum 1,500 square feet and a maximum of 3,999 square feet; and

(3) 40 percent for all nonresidential structures.

(i) Lot size. Minimum lot sizes must conform to the following standards:

(1) A maximum of 105 lots with a minimum lot size of 4,000 square feet.

(2) A maximum of 135 lots with a minimum lot size of 1,500 square feet. These lots must be located a minimum of 500 feet from the southern boundary of the district.

(3) Minimum lot size is 3,000 square feet for a lot containing a private recreation center, club, or area.

(j) Stories. No maximum number of stories. (Ord. Nos. 31226; 32302)

sections.title: Open Space
Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1016.112. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A- 4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) For single family uses, a minimum of two off-street parking spaces must be provided per unit.

(c) For a private recreation center, club, or area, a minimum of five parking spaces must be provided. These parking spaces may be located within the private street subject to engineering approval.

(d) A minimum of 35 guest parking spaces must be provided within the Property. These spaces must be provided in addition to the off-street parking requirement for residential uses and for a private recreation center, club, or area. If guest parking is provided as on-street parking, it may only be parallel indented parking along a Type A private street and subject to engineering approval.

(e) Except as provided in this subsection, a parking space in an enclosed structure that can be directly entered from a private street must be at least 20 feet from the property line abutting the private street. For a 1,500 square foot lot, a parking space in an enclosed structure that can be directly entered from a private street may be five feet from the abutting property line if:

(1) the garage door has a remote automatic control installed that is maintained in working condition; and

(2) no portion of the garage door encroaches into the abutting private street when it opens or closes. (Ord. 31226)

sections.title: Fence Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1016.113. FENCE STANDARDS.

(a) Except as provided in this section, fences must be constructed and maintained in accordance with the requirements of Section 51A-4.602.

(b) A maximum six-foot-high perimeter fence must be provided as shown on the conceptual plan.

(1) Northern and eastern perimeter (Samuell Boulevard and Hunnicut Road). Where not adjacent to residential lots, the required fences along these perimeters must be of open fence materials such as wrought iron, otherwise it may be a solid masonry fence.

(2) Southern perimeter. The required fence along this perimeter must be a solid wood fence.

(3) Western perimeter. The required fence along this perimeter may be a solid wood fence. This fence may be erected in sections as each single family dwelling unit along this

perimeter is developed. Each section of this fence must be installed prior to the final inspection on a building permit of each single family dwelling unit along this perimeter.

(c) Fences are prohibited along the property line of individual residential lots that abut a mews courtyard or an open space.

(d) To prevent visual monotony, at least 25 percent of the length of any solid masonry fence that is 200 linear feet or longer and located along a public street must have decorative elements, offsets, or openings. These changes must be spread out at even intervals over the length of the fence.

(e) Fences must be maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance. (Ord. 31226)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1016.114. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 31226)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1016.115. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(1) Landscape plan. A landscape plan must be submitted with a development plan and approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of any building permit to authorize work in this district. If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the landscape plan, the text of this article controls.

(2) Site trees.

(A) In general. Site trees must comply with the landscape plan.

(B) Single family uses.

(i) For all residential lots with a minimum size of 4,000 square feet, minimum one tree per lot.

(ii) For all residential lots with a minimum size of 1,500 square feet, one tree for every 4,000 square feet of site area within that designated phase specified on the landscape plan.

(iii) A minimum of one street tree for every 100 linear feet of street frontage within 10 feet of private street curb.

(C) All other uses. Site trees must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(D) Existing trees. Existing trees may count as site trees in accordance with Article X.

(3) Street trees.

(A) Samuell Boulevard. A minimum of one tree per every 100 feet of street frontage must be provided. All existing living and healthy protected trees on the property within 50 feet of the right-of-way, must be retained in their original location unless a defense to prosecution applies under Section 51A-10.140 of Article X, or for the purpose of a separate building permit for a single family dwelling.

(B) Hunnicut Road. A minimum of one tree per every 50 feet of street frontage must be provided. Where a conflict with overhead utility exists, two small trees may replace one large or medium tree.

(4) Open space planting. A minimum of 25 percent of any open space that is also designated as a detention area must be maintained as a habitat preservation and restoration area designated for native prairie vegetation management. This habitat preservation and restoration area must be contiguous and must be shown on the landscape plan. A maintenance plan with information for grass and forb species, site preparation, planting, and site management must be provided to the building official prior to site preparation. Initial seeding of the habitat preservation and restoration area must begin within six months from the completion of infrastructure development of the detention area.

(5) Urban forest conservation. The provisions for tree protection, removal, and replacement, in Article X, apply to this district.

(b) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 31226)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1016.116. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 31226)

sections.title: Street And Sidewalk Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1016.117. STREET AND SIDEWALK STANDARDS.

(a) Street standards.

(1) Applicability. These standards apply to all proposed private streets and mews courtyards shown on the conceptual plan.

(2) Private streets and mews courtyard sections. All proposed private streets and mews courtyards must comply with this section and with the street section (Exhibit 1016B), if applicable. If there is a conflict between the text of this section and the street section, the text of this section controls.

(A) Private streets. Except as provided in this subparagraph, private streets must comply with Section 51A-4.211(5).

(i) Type A. Minimum right-of-way is 50 feet with a minimum pavement of 26 feet.

(ii) Type B. Minimum right-of-way is 28 feet with a minimum pavement of 26 feet.

(B) Mews courtyard.

(i) All mews courtyards providing pedestrian access to residential lots must have a minimum width of 32 feet.

(ii) A mews courtyard must be platted as a separate common area or private street and maintained by a homeowner’s association.

(b) Sidewalk standards.

(1) Type A. A minimum five-foot unobstructed sidewalk must be provided along both sides of all proposed Type A private streets.

(2) Type B. No sidewalk is required.

(3) Mews courtyard. A minimum four-foot unobstructed sidewalk must be provided along each side of every mews courtyard to provide pedestrian connection to all the dwelling units abutting the mews courtyard.

(4) Perimeter sidewalks. A minimum six-foot unobstructed sidewalk must be provided along Samuell Boulevard and Hunnicut Road. (Ord. 31226)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1016.118. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 31226)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1016.119. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 31226)
